title: Finite-field internal Hom finiteness over an arbitrary ground field
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime and $k$ a field of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. Let $X$ be a separated scheme of finite type over $k$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], and let $A$ be a finite field of characteristic $\ell$, with its discrete topology. Regard $\underline A$ as a condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and let $A_X=p_X^*\underline A$ be its coefficient sheaf [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], equivalently the constant ring sheaf $A$ on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$. Let $P,Q$ be $A_X$-module complexes with cohomology vanishing outside finite intervals and with every cohomology sheaf constructible in the finite constant local model sense [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: on a finite constructible locally closed stratification each sheaf is pro-étale locally constant with finite-dimensional $A$-values. Then the ambient derived internal Hom
$$
R\mathcal Hom_{A_X}(P,Q)
$$
[sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] has cohomology vanishing outside a finite interval, with every cohomology sheaf constructible in this same finite constant local model sense. The ground field $k$ is not required to be finite, perfect or separably closed.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.13 with coefficient ring R=A and ideal m=0, together with Definition 6.5.1 and Lemma 6.3.16; finite-type schemes over a field are quasi-excellent and ell is invertible. This is the finite-field coefficient specialization, not the integral assertion.

proof.text: Use the constant coefficient ring sheaf $A_T$ on every scheme $T$ below. The identification $p_T^*\underline A\cong A_T$ asserted in the statement is checked as follows. Since $A$ is discrete, $\underline A(S)=C(S,A)$ is the ring of locally constant functions on the profinite set $S$, which is the sheafification of the constant presheaf $A$ on $*_{\mathrm{proét}}$. By [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point] (3)–(4), $p_T^*$ is inverse image along $u_T\colon S\mapsto T[S]$, that is, sheafification after left Kan extension; as both are left adjoints, $p_T^*$ of a sheafified presheaf is the sheafification of the Kan extension of that presheaf. For $V\in T_{\mathrm{proét}}$ the indexing category of maps $V\to T[S]$ over $T$ has the terminal object $V\to T[*]=T$, so it is connected and the Kan extension of the constant presheaf $A$ is the constant presheaf $A$. Hence $p_T^*\underline A$ is the constant ring sheaf $A_T$, with the constant ring operations. Since $A$ is a finite field, finite-dimensional, finitely generated and finitely presented $A$-modules are the same finite modules. Consequently the finite constant local model definition in [sk-def-sfb-constructible] is exactly the intrinsic finite-coefficient constructibility used below. Write $\mathcal B(T)$ for the complexes with this constructible cohomology in a finite interval. The field $k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0,k$), and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is quasi-compact with its single point; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian. Every open subscheme of a Noetherian scheme is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. An immersion is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft]. Closed immersions are quasi-compact (inverse images of quasi-compact opens are closed subsets of those opens); an open immersion in a Noetherian scheme is quasi-compact by the preceding open-subscheme result applied on affine opens. Hence all open and closed immersions used below are finite type. Their sources are again finite type over $k$: on affine charts this says that a finitely generated algebra over a finitely generated $k$-algebra is finitely generated, by adjoining both finite sets of generators. They are therefore Noetherian too. Such schemes are quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]; the quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness required of the morphisms below follow from [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. No assumption on perfection, finiteness or separable closedness of $k$ is used. The ambient categories and internal Hom of the statement are those of the cited ringed-site nodes: module objects over the ring object $A_T$ of $\Sh(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ are exactly sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_T$, with the same morphisms, and the Layer-B derived tensor product of [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] is the K-flat derived tensor product of module sheaves. Hence its internal Hom, being a right adjoint of $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_T}-$, is canonically isomorphic, by uniqueness of right adjoints, to the ringed-site $R\mathcal Hom_{A_T}$ used in steps 9–11.

source.place: §6.7 hypotheses; finite-type specialization of the schemes used in Lemmas 6.7.11 and 6.7.13

proof.text: On the Noetherian, hence qcqs, scheme $T$, the affine-local convention in [lem-sfb-discrete-noetherian-constructible-serre] agrees with the global convention defining $\mathcal B(T)$. A global partition restricts to any affine open by intersecting its strata with that open. Conversely, choose a finite affine cover and its witnessing partitions. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-stratification-local-gluing-core]: each resulting global stratum factors by an actual scheme morphism through one chosen local stratum. Pull back its trivializing cover along that morphism; inverse image of a constant $A$-module sheaf is the constant sheaf of the same finite-dimensional module. Thus the refined partition has the required finite constant local models. Since $A$ is Noetherian, the weak-Serre statement now supplies zero, kernels, cokernels and extensions in precisely this global convention.

source.place: Tag 095E, lemma-constructible-quasi-compact-quasi-separated, finite affine-cover refinement; proetale.tex Tags 09AJ, definition-constructible, and 09B5, lemma-constructible-serre.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-cohomology-in-weak-serre-subcategory] with the abelian category of $A_T$-module sheaves and with its strictly full subcategory of constructible sheaves from step 2. Its zero, kernel, cokernel and extension hypotheses were established there. Its bounded version gives exactly closure of $\mathcal B(T)$ under shifts and distinguished triangles.

For a scheme morphism $v:T'\to T$, inverse image is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact]: the coefficient ring pulls back to the same constant ring, so the module inverse image has this underlying exact abelian inverse image. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] termwise gives $H^r(v^*K)\cong v^*H^r(K)$ and preserves its finite vanishing interval. For constructible cohomology, [lem-weil-pbc-module-constructible-pullback] pulls back finite stratifications and finite presentations. Over the finite constant ring $A$, each finite presentation matrix has only finitely many locally constant entries; refining its pro-étale cover to make these entries constant turns it into a scalar matrix. Its cokernel is a finite-dimensional constant $A$-module there. Thus the pulled-back local models are precisely the required finite constant local models, and $v^*$ preserves $\mathcal B$. This applies to open and closed ordinary inverse images.

source.place: Tag 04JC, exact inverse image; constructible pullback interface

proof.text:
For any finite-type morphism $f:T\to V$ between the finite-type $k$-schemes used here, ordinary pro-étale $Rf_*$ preserves $\mathcal B$. To see all hypotheses, choose for $C\in\mathcal B(T)$ a bounded constructible étale origin $C_0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin]. Since $A$ is annihilated by $\ell$ and $p\ne\ell$, the integer $\ell$ is invertible in $k$. Thus [thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility], which allows arbitrary fields and finite rings, gives $Rf_{\mathrm{ét},*}C_0\in D^b_c(V_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$. The morphism is qcqs as checked in step 1, and $C_0$ is bounded below, so [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] identifies
$$Rf_{\mathrm{proét},*}C\cong\nu_V^*Rf_{\mathrm{ét},*}C_0.$$
The interval-preserving constructible comparison in the first cited node puts the right side in $\mathcal B(V)$. In particular this proves the ordinary direct-image finiteness needed for each open or closed immersion below; it does not assume a cohomological-dimension bound on the ground field.

source.place: Theorem 6.7.1, Lemma 6.7.2 with R=A and m=0; comparison Lemma 5.4.3; Stacks Tags 09AL and 099R

proof.text:
Let $g:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion among these schemes, with open complement $h:W\hookrightarrow T$, and let $M\in\mathcal B(T)$. Apply [lem-exc-proetale-support-triangle] to obtain
$$g_*Rg^!M\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow Rh_*h^*M\longrightarrow g_*Rg^!M[1].$$
Here $T$ is Noetherian and $A$ is finite, exactly the hypotheses of that ambient support triangle. Step 4 gives $h^*M\in\mathcal B(W)$; step 5 gives $Rh_*h^*M\in\mathcal B(T)$; steps 2–3 and the triangle give $g_*Rg^!M\in\mathcal B(T)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], $g^*g_*\cong\mathrm{id}$ and $g_*$ is exact. Applying the constructible-preserving exact $g^*$ of step 4 therefore gives $Rg^!M\in\mathcal B(Z)$. The complement is quasi-compact because $T$ is Noetherian. This proves the closed-support case inside this argument, without introducing another node.

Every sheaf of $A_T$-modules is flat. Here is the elementary argument that permits use of flat-sheaf generation without an additional finite-Tor hypothesis. Regard the coefficient ring as the sheafification of the constant ring presheaf $A$. By [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-tensor], tensoring two $A_T$-module sheaves can be computed by sheafifying the presheaf $U\mapsto F(U)\otimes_A G(U)$. A monomorphism of sheaves is injective on sections by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact]. For every object $U$, choose an $A$-basis of $F(U)$; tensoring an injection with $F(U)$ is then a direct sum of copies of that injection, hence injective. Exact sheafification, again [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact], preserves this monomorphism. Tensor is right exact (it represents bilinear maps, so is a left adjoint), and is therefore exact. This proves flatness even though a constructible sheaf need not be locally free on all of $T$.

source.place: Tag 0GMW, lemma-sheafification-tensor, applied to the constant presheaf A; exact sheafification, lemma-sheafification-exact; vector-space basis calculation

proof.text:
Apply clauses (1) and (2) of [det-sf-flat-model-generation] to each constructible sheaf $F$ on $X$: its flatness was proved in step 7 and $X$ is Noetherian by step 1. It follows that $F$ is a finite iterated extension of $a_!L$ for locally closed strata $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ and locally constant sheaves $L$ with finite projective $A$-values, hence finite-dimensional $A$-values. Use precisely that node's convention: factor $a$ as $S\xrightarrow{j}Z\xrightarrow{g}X$, with $j$ open in the scheme-theoretic closure and $g$ closed, and put $a_!L=g_*j_!L$. Each short exact extension in the sheaf filtration gives a distinguished triangle after placing the sheaves in degree zero, by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle]. Both $Z$ and $S$ satisfy step 1. For the bounded complex $P$, the triangles of [lem-pc-derived-lower-truncation-step-triangle] give a finite construction from the $H^r(P)[-r]$: if $H^r(P)=0$ outside $[u,v]$, start with $\tau_{\ge v+1}P=0$ and successively use
$$H^r(P)[-r]\longrightarrow\tau_{\ge r}P\longrightarrow\tau_{\ge r+1}P\longrightarrow H^r(P)[-r+1]$$
for $r=v,v-1,\ldots,u$, ending at $\tau_{\ge u}P\cong P$. Consequently $P$ is obtained by finitely many shifts and extensions from these $g_*j_!L$.

source.place: Lemmas 6.3.3 and 6.3.9 and the filtering argument of Lemma 6.7.13; existing flat-sheaf generation used only in clauses (1)–(2)

proof.text: For later use let $L$ be locally constant with finite-dimensional $A$-values on $S$ and let $N\in\mathcal B(S)$. Then $R\mathcal Hom_{A_S}(L,N)\in\mathcal B(S)$. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] allows restriction of the ambient derived internal Hom to every object of a pro-étale cover trivializing $L$. On a member on which $L\cong A^d$, the restricted Hom is $N^{\oplus d}$: by tensor–Hom adjunction the internal Hom out of the tensor unit $A$ is the identity, and a finite direct sum in the first argument becomes a finite product, equal here to a finite direct sum. Thus the cohomology vanishes outside the very same finite interval as that of $N$, independently of $d$. Moreover $H^rR\mathcal Hom(L,N)=\mathcal Hom(L,H^rN)$, and the basis calculation gives $\mathcal Hom(L,H^rN)=L^\vee\otimes H^rN$ locally. On any stratum trivializing $H^rN$ pro-étale locally, intersect that cover with a trivializing cover of $L$; these sheaves then have finite-dimensional constant values, and so does their tensor product. The original finite stratification for $H^rN$ therefore witnesses constructibility of this cohomology sheaf. No assertion that restriction to an arbitrary closed stratum commutes with derived Hom is being used.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.13, locally constant calculation; Stacks Tag 08JB, lemma-restriction-RHom-to-U

proof.text:
Compute the Hom for a generator from step 8, keeping its open-then-closed factorization. Apply [lem-weil-stratum-ambient-hom] first to the closed immersion $g:Z\hookrightarrow X$ (take the subsequent open immersion to be the identity), and then to the open immersion $j:S\hookrightarrow Z$ (take the preceding closed immersion to be the identity). Since the ambient right adjoint of open extension by zero is the exact restriction $j^*$, these give
$$\begin{aligned}
R\mathcal Hom_{A_X}(g_*j_!L,Q)
&\cong Rg_*R\mathcal Hom_{A_Z}(j_!L,Rg^!Q)\\
&\cong Rg_*Rj_*R\mathcal Hom_{A_S}(L,j^*Rg^!Q).
\end{aligned}$$
In the open specialization the closed factor is the identity; its direct image has identity right adjoint, since $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathrm{id}(K),M)=\operatorname{Hom}(K,\mathrm{id}(M))$. The definition of $Rs^!$ in [lem-weil-stratum-ambient-hom] therefore gives $j^!=j^{-1}=j^*$. Exactness of $g_*$, so $Rg_*=g_*$, is included in [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-open-closed-recollement], applied to the finite constant coefficient ring. Only its exact sheaf direct image is used here; the closed exceptional functor is the ambient right adjoint already used in step 6. Every base is Noetherian by step 1 and every open complement is quasi-compact, as required by these two cited statements. Step 6 gives $Rg^!Q\in\mathcal B(Z)$, step 4 gives $j^*Rg^!Q\in\mathcal B(S)$, and step 9 gives constructibility and boundedness of the innermost Hom. Applying step 5 to $j$ and then $g$ proves $R\mathcal Hom(g_*j_!L,Q)\in\mathcal B(X)$. We never exchange the two factors of $a$, and need no assertion about independence of its factorization.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.13, adjunction calculation, expanded for the canonical open-then-closed stratum generators; Lemma 6.7.11

proof.text: Fix $Q$ and propagate step 10 through the finite construction of $P$ in step 8. The bifunctor sends triangles to triangles contravariantly in its first variable and sends a shift in that variable to the opposite shift in the value by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. Thus the zero object, each generator, each shifted generator, and each successive extension have Hom into $Q$ in $\mathcal B(X)$, using the closure established in steps 2–3. Induction first over each finite extension filtration of a sheaf and then over the finite truncation tower of $P$ proves $R\mathcal Hom_{A_X}(P,Q)\in\mathcal B(X)$. By the definition of $\mathcal B$ in step 1 this is exactly the two claimed conclusions: a finite cohomological interval and constructibility in the specified finite constant local model sense. The empty scheme and zero complexes give zero throughout.

Ensures open strata and open complements stay Noetherian and quasi-compact.

Supplies quasi-separatedness for the comparison theorem.
Supplies qcqs for the ordinary direct-image comparison on the finite-type strata.

Pulls finite stratifications and finite presentations back along the immersions.
Finite-ring comparison identifies intrinsic bounded constructibility with bounded constructible etale origin.
Ordinary finite-coefficient direct-image finiteness over an arbitrary field; the unit lower-star lemma only treats adic and rational coefficients.
Transports the ordinary finite-ring etale direct-image finiteness to the pro-etale ambient category.
The ambient closed-support triangle, used to prove constructibility of the closed exceptional inverse image rather than assume it.
Exact closed direct image and g^*g_*=id finish the closed-support calculation.
The constant-presheaf tensor formula proves flatness over the coefficient field by a basis calculation.
Exact sheafification and sectionwise monomorphisms justify the elementary flatness calculation.
Clauses (1)–(2) give finite stratified extension filtrations of flat constructible sheaves, with general finite coefficients and no special ground field.
The explicit generic truncation triangle gives a finite construction of P from its cohomology sheaves.
Ambient ringed-site Hom commutes with slice restriction, shifts and triangles; no constructible-preservation is assumed.
